description:
FILED s514 (Fable, 2026-10-10 10:1x) as the umbrella for s514a member 1, from the production review item 5 re-ordered by measured value: the Digest pair flips an EVERYDAY row (modules/Digest-SHA-MD5.pl, blessed `not-supported.md#dynaloader--xs-binary-extensions -- Digest::MD5/SHA are XS; pclxs is parked`), so it comes before Storable.  LAYER (rule 9a): a digest is a thing a user can write in plain Perl -> lib/ shims, nothing in Pl/ or cl/.  API = perl's (functional md5/md5_hex/md5_base64, sha1..sha512 + _hex/_base64, hmac_sha*; OO new/add/addfile/digest/hexdigest/b64digest/reset/clone; base64 without padding; wide chars die perl-shaped).  A vendored pure-Perl implementation (Digest::Perl::MD5, Digest::SHA::PurePerl -- Perl license) is allowed with its header kept and a PCLLicense.pm exclusion by name.  ORACLE = perl's XS modules on this box (byte-identical digests).  BAR: guard Pl/t/digest-shim-01.t (~30 rows, perl's answers at run time, inverse-verified), the everyday row FIXED (114 -> 115, baseline edited BY EDIT citing s514a + #2947), speed of md5_hex / sha256_hex of 1 MB vs perl REPORTED (not a bar).  Brief: briefs-and-rules-for-claude-subagents/s514/s514a-prompt.md.

=== DONE (s514a) ===
lib/Digest/MD5.pm + lib/Digest/SHA.pm written fresh in plain Perl (32-bit masked steps, SHA-512 in 32-bit halves, HMAC padded byte by byte -- #1040).  Byte-identical to the XS modules on every probe; dies by name: Digest::MD5::context, getstate/putstate/dump/load, partial-byte add_bits.  Guard Pl/t/digest-shim-01.t 40 rows (39 fail on 4d2fc9f0).  everyday modules/Digest-SHA-MD5 FIXED: EVERYDAY 114 -> 115 of 122 (row edited out of baselines/everyday-baseline.tsv).  Speed on 1 MB (load ~4.7): md5 0.465 s vs perl 0.001, sha1 0.894 vs 0.001, sha256 1.912 vs 0.003, sha512 4.368 vs 0.002 (~400x / ~640x / ~2000x) -- in docs/shipped-modules.md; the runtime-primitive follow-up is Fable's.  Commit 21007ede.
subject: SHIM: Digest::MD5 + Digest::SHA in pure Perl (lib/Digest/MD5.pm, lib/Digest/SHA.pm) -- the everyday program modules/Digest-SHA-MD5.pl is a blessed DIFF row (XS, pclxs parked) and the review (docs/production-readiness-review-s513.md) lists Digest::MD5 among the production unblockers; batch s514a member 1
